sources.title: Claude 2
sources.evidence: July 11, 2023 launch announcement names Claude 2, makes it available through the API and public chat beta, and specifies prompts up to 100K tokens and text responses. Reopened on October 27, 2026; the announcement supplies no nominal total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Model Card and Evaluations for Claude Models
sources.evidence: Reopened the original 14-page card on October 27, 2026. It identifies Anthropic and Transformer training with unsupervised learning, RLHF and Constitutional AI, but no nominal total or active count or dense/MoE classification. Figure 6, page 7, has a parameter-axis plot for earlier research preference/language models and a separate Claude-model accuracy bar chart; the numeric axis is not a Claude 2 size disclosure.

sources.title: Model Card and Evaluations for Claude Models, with Claude 2.1 appendix
sources.evidence: Reinspected the full text of the official PDF freshly fetched on October 27, 2026 at 10:08:59 UTC through the shared primary-source cache. The November 21, 2023 appendix explicitly names Claude 2.0 and says 2.1 is not a new base model, but neither version receives a parameter count. It states 2.0 was trained for 200K context but launched with 100K product support; 2.1 enabled full 200K support.

sources.title: The Claude 3 Model Family: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, with 3.5 addenda
sources.evidence: Reinspected full text of the official 46.8 MB PDF freshly fetched on October 27, 2026 at 10:09:00 UTC. The Claude 3/3.5 card and addenda provide Claude 2/2.0 performance comparisons, including multilingual MMLU Table 5 and QuALITY Table 6, without total or activated-parameter columns. Section 5.8 qualitatively orders Claude 3 model sizes without any Claude 2.0 size disclosure.

sources.title: Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy, Version 1.0
sources.evidence: Effective September 19, 2023, page 5 explicitly classifies then-current Claude 2 as ASL-2. Its containment measures treat model weights as core intellectual property, restrict access by job function and secure them against unsanctioned release. This is contemporaneous weight-access evidence rather than an inference from API hosting.

sources.title: Commercial Terms of Service
sources.evidence: The accessed terms are effective June 17, 2025, before Claude 2.0 retirement. They grant conditional service use and expressly do not grant rights to the other party's intellectual property except as stated; they are not a public model-weight license.

sources.title: Model deprecations
sources.evidence: Current retirement history explicitly maps Claude 2 to claude-2.0 and records retirement on July 21, 2025, separately from claude-2.1. Retired endpoints are no longer available for use.

sources.title: Introducing Claude 2.1
sources.evidence: November 21, 2023 announcement names Claude 2.0 as the preceding model and announces API tool use as a new beta feature alongside Claude 2.1. It cannot establish the same native feature for 2.0.

sources.title: Write a custom parser Lambda function in Amazon Bedrock Agents
sources.evidence: Official Bedrock Agents documentation includes an explicitly labeled Claude 2.0 orchestration parser that extracts function_call and scratchpad content from raw model output. This establishes a provider-orchestrated integration, but does not establish native Anthropic API tool-call or extended-thinking support.

sources.title: Supported foundation models in Amazon Bedrock (indexed historical table)
sources.evidence: The complete indexed primary table lists Claude 2 / anthropic.claude-v2 with Text input and Text, Chat output, separately from Claude 2.1. The indexed table is historical (search metadata approximately 1.4 years old); direct opening now redirects to a relocation notice. Used only for last-documented modalities, not current availability.

sources.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code
sources.evidence: February 24, 2025 announcement describes Claude 3.7 as the first hybrid reasoning model and explains its optional extended-thinking mode. This later feature is not evidence that Claude 2.0 exposes a dedicated reasoning mode.

sources.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet System Card
sources.evidence: Reinspected the full text of the official PDF freshly fetched on October 27, 2026 at 10:08:59 UTC. Its model descriptions and later comparison/evaluation tables contain no Claude 2.0 nominal total or activated-parameter disclosure; no parameter-count column or named size-bearing Claude 2.0 base relationship was found.

sources.title: Many-shot Jailbreaking
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27, 2026. The study evaluates Claude 2.0, but its size experiments use qualitative model labels. Appendix H, pages 28-29, discusses research models up to 52B and explicitly states in footnote 5 that they belong to an older lineage than Claude 2.0. The 52B number is therefore not a nominal Claude 2.0 count or a supported base-model inference; no Claude 2.0 active count appears.

sources.title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
sources.evidence: Freshly downloaded and text-inspected October 27, 2026 after the web reader rejected the 20.6 MB HTML size. Its one-layer Transformer with a 512-neuron MLP and sparse-autoencoder feature counts are research models, while Claude 2 is used to explain features and predict activations. Neither those dimensions nor sparse active-feature counts describe Claude 2.0 total or active parameters.

sources.title: Anthropic Business Breakdown and Founding Story
sources.evidence: Checked as a secondary lead on October 27, 2026. Its claimed Claude 2 size of 860 million links to a Product Hunt explainer, not an Anthropic specification. Followed that citation; no developer count was established.

sources.title: Claude 2: What it is and how to use Claude AI
sources.evidence: Followed Contrary Research's size citation on October 27, 2026. This secondary explainer asserts 860 million parameters without a supporting Anthropic specification and gives July 2022 as the Claude 2 release in the same passage, conflicting with the July 2023 primary release. It does not establish a verified nominal count and is not adopted.

name.note: Original public name is Claude 2; later card and retirement documentation identify this exact revision as Claude 2.0 / claude-2.0.

developer.note: Explicitly identified as developer in the original model card.

family.note: Normalized family key for the card's Claude model lineage.

release_date.note: Dated announcement states public chat access begins that day and announces API access. This is the original release, before the November 2.1 update.

open_weights.note: Contemporaneous Claude 2 security policy explicitly restricts weight access and protects weights against unsanctioned release; service terms grant no general intellectual-property rights.

license.note: License category supported by protected model intellectual property and contractual service access; not an SPDX license name or a claim that the June 2025 terms were the launch-day terms.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found no developer-published nominal total or size-bearing base lineage for Claude 2.0. Figure 6 and Many-shot Jailbreaking's 52B experiment concern separate research models; the interpretability paper uses Claude 2 as an evaluator. The secondary 860M lead lacks an Anthropic specification.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked active parameters separately in the original card, 2.1 appendix, later Claude 3/3.5 and 3.7 comparisons, and research leads. No Claude 2.0 activated-parameter count or column was found; sparse-autoencoder activations are not model active parameters, and no total-equality or density assumption is made.

architecture.note: Original card explicitly identifies Transformer architecture. Dense versus MoE and detailed topology remain undisclosed.

context_window.note: Released 2.0 product limit. Later appendix says 2.0 was trained for 200K, but only 100K was supported at launch; full 200K support belongs to 2.1.

modalities.note: Launch describes text prompts and generated text. Historical official provider table explicitly lists Text input and Text/Chat output; Chat is normalized to text.

reasoning.note: General reasoning benchmark improvements and scaffolded scratchpad text do not establish a dedicated reasoning mode. Later 3.7 extended thinking is not transferred to 2.0; a categorical feature flag remains unresolved.

tool_call.note: Scope differs across sources: the original card permits search-tool integrations, AWS documents a 2.0 function-call parser, and Anthropic introduces native API tool use with 2.1. A provider-independent native tool-call boolean for 2.0 is not established.

description.value: Anthropic's July 2023 Claude text model, using a Transformer architecture and a 100K-token public context window. The claude-2.0 API model was retired on July 21, 2025.
description.note: Replaces the generic historical description with exact release, architecture, context and retirement facts.

patch.description: Anthropic's July 2023 Claude text model, using a Transformer architecture and a 100K-token public context window. The claude-2.0 API model was retired on July 21, 2025.
patch.notes: Nominal total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; the 52B research-model count is not a Claude 2.0 specification. Transformer architecture is documented; dense versus MoE is not. Claude 2.0's publicly supported context was 100K, although the later model-card appendix discloses 200K training context; 2.1 enabled full 200K support. Claude 2.0 retired from the Anthropic API on July 21, 2025. Dedicated reasoning and native tool-call flags remain unresolved; Bedrock Agents' scaffolded function-call parser is distinct from Anthropic's later API tool-use feature.

sources.label: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null nominal total and active counts after reopening the original release/card, independently inspecting freshly downloaded 2.1, 3/3.5 and 3.7 cards, and running targeted first-party total/active/interpretability searches. Resolved the separate research-model parameter axis in Figure 6, the older-lineage 52B models in Many-shot Jailbreaking, and the one-layer/autoencoder models in Towards Monosemanticity. Traced a secondary 860M claim through Contrary to an unsupported Product Hunt explainer; no developer count or size-bearing lineage supports it. All nonparameter assessments are preserved.
